unit.title: Functions as a Unifying Language
unit.act: Act XII - Organizing algebra around input and output
unit.role: Consolidate earlier relationships into function language without preempting full Precalculus theory.
unit.governingQuestion: How can one input-output framework organize the algebraic families already studied?
unit.storyArc: Relations become functions when each input has one output. Function notation separates evaluation from solving; domain and range collect restrictions and outputs; piecewise functions and arithmetic unify earlier examples.
outcomes: Determine whether a relation is a function.
Evaluate functions and solve output equations.
Determine domain and range from formulas, graphs, and contexts.
Interpret graph behavior and piecewise rules.
Combine functions arithmetically while tracking domain.
unit.investigation: Choose among linear, quadratic, rational, radical, and exponential models for unlabeled data or graphs.
unit.mastery: Students move among table, graph, formula, and context and distinguish evaluation from solving.
